title: Ex-Trump Aide Bolton Says 'I'm Sorry' in Court
summary: Have you ever kept a secret that you weren't supposed to have? John Bolton, who used to be President Trump's national security adviser (someone who helps keep the country safe), did something like that — but with top-secret government papers. On Friday, June 26, 2026, Bolton stood in a courtroom in Greenbelt, Maryland, and said, "I am sorry for it." He pleaded guilty (admitted he did it) to keeping secret information that could have hurt the country. He could go to prison for up to 5 years and pay a $2.25 million fine. Bolton used to send secret messages to his family through texts and email. Some of those secrets were later stolen by hackers from Iran. Some people think the government is only going after Bolton because he criticized President Trump. But a former government lawyer named Stacey Young said this case is different — it's real. Bolton's own lawyer said he was being a "real leader" by admitting his mistake. What do you think — should people who handle secrets be punished if they mess up?
why_it_matters: This shows how important it is to keep promises and not share things that aren't ours, whether it's a friend's secret or classified information.

background_read: John Bolton (a former U.S. national security adviser) worked for President Donald Trump (who was the U.S. president from 2017 to 2021).
Governments keep many things secret to stay safe, and people with access to these secrets must follow strict rules.
If they break those rules, even by accident, it can be a crime because secrets could fall into the hands of other countries, like Iran (a country in the Middle East).
